title: The earth-formed animals differ from the earlier water-born ones
english: For in many ways, the Father says, it is possible to discern the difference and unlikeness of these animals and birds. First, by saying, “And the Lord God formed still from the earth” (Genesis 2:19). For we do not find anything formed by God except the human being. Again, by saying “still,” the Scripture shows that certain other animals and birds are being prophesied here, different from the earlier ones. For it is not written that the first birds came into being from the earth, but from the waters. These, however, came into being from the earth—or rather, they were formed by God’s own hand, and not according to command.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG 18 In Genesim de creatione u01-open
orientation: Eustathius is answering the philosopher's question about the creation of animals and humanity in Genesis, and here he begins to distinguish the animals formed from the earth in Genesis 2 from those created earlier from the waters.
